v.why: Reducing a very strong L2 penalty (alpha near 1) relieves severe underfitting and gives large gains, as seen in runs 14 and 20.

With a tiny learning rate the 243 epochs are undertrained, so a larger step helps, whereas at high rates it destabilizes.
Lowering an excessively high learning rate restores stable training and gives large gains (runs 52, 57).
Raising an already large learning rate leads to divergence and accuracy loss.
Deeper networks are harder to optimize at large learning rates, so adding layers hurts there.
Removing layers makes training more stable when the learning rate is high.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening them helps more than widening already wide ones.
Shrinking an already narrow network cuts capacity and reduces accuracy.
Very small batches give noisy updates, so a modest increase stabilizes training more than it would at larger batch sizes.
